candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether values in this table represent enforceable discharge limits, calculated instream concentrations for reasonable-potential screening, or non-operative analytical outputs determines which numeric values are eligible for compliance comparison in Purpose A.

Interpretation of ambient versus effluent concentration columns, and whether blank cells denote unmeasured, zero, or not-applicable values, affects limit derivation in Purpose A and whether missing ambient/effluent evidence is documented no-data versus unresolved in Purpose C.

This formula links reported effluent concentration to an acute instream waste concentration; a different reading of the multiplier, units, or whether it is binding would change the derived numeric limit used for comparison.

Method quantification limit values govern whether reported measurements are comparable to numeric limits (A), whether monitoring must achieve a stated detection/reporting level (B), and how non-detect or below-MQL results are classified versus missing evidence (C).

These sentinel entries may denote a non-applicable criterion rather than a literal numeric limit; treating them as operative limits versus exclusions changes which criterion column governs compliance comparison for a parameter.

Multiple parallel criteria families (acute aquatic, chronic aquatic, human health, TMDL need) appear on the same row; which column is controlling for a given discharge point and monitoring period determines the applicable enforceable limit.

Pollutant form and naming determine which reported measurements map to this row; misalignment between dissolved versus total speciation would change applicable limits, monitoring expectations, and missing-evidence classification.

The total-recoverable form carries different criterion values than the dissolved form on the same page; selecting the wrong speciation changes limit applicability, monitoring obligation matching, and how absent results are interpreted.

The parenthetical (P) may indicate provisional or permit-specific status; whether that qualifier makes associated criteria enforceable, advisory, or conditionally applicable would change limit selection and monitoring requirements.

The (P) qualifier on a dissolved selenium line may signal provisional criteria or special permit conditions, affecting which numeric limits are enforceable and whether associated monitoring is required.

This row is conditional on sulfate concentration exceeding 500 mg/l; interpretation of when that condition is met determines which selenium limit applies, whether conditional monitoring is required, and how to classify missing selenium results when sulfate evidence is absent.

The same pollutant row presents multiple numeric criteria (e.g., 1.4 acute aquatic and 0.77 chronic aquatic) alongside calculated instream values; choosing acute versus chronic or calculated versus tabulated criteria would change the enforceable limit used for exceedance determination.

The Need/TMDL column entries marked N/A may indicate that no TMDL-based limit applies or that TMDL need was not established; interpreting N/A as exclusion versus placeholder affects whether a TMDL-derived limit must be considered.

Blank MQL and effluent/ambient cells combined with zero calculated columns and a finite irrigation criterion (1000) create ambiguity between no-discharge/no-data and a potentially applicable numeric criterion, affecting both limit selection and missing-evidence classification.
